 Flight disruptions intensified across the U.S. on Tuesday, with nearly 1,900 flights delayed and more than 50 canceled as low clouds threatened operations at several major airports.
 FlightAware listed 1,886 delays involving flights within, into or out of the nation as of 6:45 p.m. EDT. The tracking service also reported 52 cancellations tied to U.S. operations. 
 Worldwide, FlightAware listed more than 12,000 delays and 730 cancellations.
 The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said low clouds could delay flights at Denver International Airport, San Diego International Airport, and Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. The agency did not attribute every delay or cancellation recorded by FlightAware to weather.
 The latest figures mark a substantial increase from earlier on Tuesday morning, when FlightAware reported about 800 U.S.-related delays and 32 cancellations.
 Airlines typically adjust schedules throughout the day as weather, air traffic volume, aircraft availability, and crew scheduling affect operations. Travelers were urged to check with their airlines for the latest information on departures, arrivals and possible rebooking options.
 The FAA’s National Airspace System dashboard provides real-time updates on airport constraints and traffic-management programs. Conditions can change quickly, particularly at airports affected by low cloud ceilings, which can reduce the number of aircraft able to land safely in a given period.
 Passengers were advised to allow extra time and monitor their flight status before heading to the airport.
